currentContext.business: Schneider Electric Infrastructure Limited (SEIL), incorporated in 2011 and part of the global Schneider Electric Group, manufactures medium-voltage switchgear, transformers and electrical distribution/automation equipment, combining global technology with domestic manufacturing and engineering capabilities. Beyond equipment supply, the Company supports customers across the full asset lifecycle - system design, commissioning, digital monitoring, predictive maintenance and modernisation - anchored by its EcoStruxure platform for digital energy management. Customers span end users, EPCs, channel partners, panel builders, distributors and contractors across utilities, industry and infrastructure segments.

currentContext.strengths: Part of the Schneider Electric Group, a global leader in energy management and automation with operations in over 100 countries, giving access to global technology expertise|One of the Group's most localised entities, combining global technology with strong domestic manufacturing and engineering capabilities aligned with the Make in India vision|Strong local footprint and partner ecosystem tailored to India's evolving infrastructure and industrial needs|Proprietary EcoStruxure platform anchoring digital energy management offerings across reliability, efficiency and lifecycle services|Long-standing customer partnerships and a growing suite of digital/recurring lifecycle services extending equipment life and customer stickiness
currentContext.strategies: Mission to advance new energy technologies that enable a more electric, digital, and sustainable world|Strategy anchored in three core pillars: Electrification (expanding access to reliable and efficient power), Digitalisation (enabling intelligent, data-driven energy systems) and Sustainability (supporting decarbonisation and resource efficiency)|Continue delivering locally engineered, digitally enabled solutions that strengthen energy management and distribution through IoT, artificial intelligence and predictive analytics|Anchor digital energy management offerings around the EcoStruxure platform to enhance customer reliability, operational efficiency and reduce environmental impact|Careful evaluation of capital expenditure plans to ensure efficient utilisation of resources and long-term value creation for stakeholders|Conserve financial resources (via no dividend for FY2025-26) to fund growth initiatives including capex, technological advancements and strategic priorities|The Company maintains a formal Dividend Distribution Policy, adopted in accordance with Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations, to ensure transparency in dividend declarations and protect investor interests; the policy document is published on the Company's website. This section does not otherwise disclose a broader capital-allocation or reinvestment philosophy beyond the existence of this policy and a separately listed Risk Management Policy.
currentContext.expansion: During FY2025-26, the Company invested in capital expenditure to enhance existing capacity of switchgears and transformers at its Vadodara Plant and of Vacuum Interrupters and VCBs at its Kolkata plant, strengthening operational capabilities in line with strategic objectives. The Company also strengthened broader manufacturing and operational capabilities to address rising demand across utilities, industrial infrastructure and digital economy segments, with investments focused on capacity expansion, new offers, efficiency enhancement, localisation and faster delivery of advanced electrical distribution and automation solutions. It expanded capabilities in digital electrical infrastructure and smart grid solutions, including substation automation, sensor-enabled transformers and connected switchgear, and strengthened engineering and execution capabilities to enable efficient delivery of complex projects across data centres, renewables, semiconductors and metro rail. Separately, the Company's KMVC Plant in Kolkata started operations in January 2026 (per BRSR disclosure).

risks.note: During FY2025-26 profitability was moderated by elevated input costs, particularly in key commodities such as copper, aluminium and steel, alongside the impact of ₹31.8 Crores from exceptional items year-on-year, even as revenue grew 9.6% year-on-year; EBITDA margin and PAT margin both declined versus the prior year.

Escalating geopolitical tensions in energy-producing regions and the Middle East have contributed to volatility in global energy prices, supply chain disruptions, inflationary pressures and tighter financial conditions; risks from geopolitical tensions, energy price volatility, trade fragmentation, rising debt and financial market uncertainties are flagged as persisting.

Global real GDP growth is projected by the IMF at 3.1% in CY2026 and 3.2% in CY2027, below recent trends and the long-term historical average, indicating a slower-growth backdrop for the capital investment cycle that underpins demand for SEIL's power infrastructure solutions.

one-line thesis: Grid power-distribution OEM (MV/LV, transformers, switchgear) + a digital/grid-automation edge (EcoStruxure, "One Digital grid" AI for DISCOMs). Order backlog ~50% up, orders +27%, but sales only +9.6% and margins squeezed by metals (gross margin 39.1%→37.5%; Cu/Al +30%, steel +10% in 12 months). A demand-side, execution/digital + services story facing the same metal-cost headwind Apar flagged.
financial scorecard: > One-off: Labour-Code exceptional ₹14cr (was ₹24cr in Q3, restructured). Detailed KPIs on the deck (slide 19) — only growth rates read on the call. Services 12%→15% of revenue (higher margin, a stated margin lever).
guidance / outlook (qualitative): India macro tailwinds: GDP ~7%; govt capex +11.5% (~₹12.2 lakh cr); power-utility outlay +20% FY27; per-capita consumption +30% by 2030 (12–15% CAGR).
Margin levers: services mix-up (+300bps possible), digital, modernization; counter metal inflation.
demand drivers / segments: Data centres: supplying power transformers (digitalized) + high-end relays + modernization to a major player; India 1.5GW → ~8GW by 2030 (~3GW in advanced rollout). DC = ~10–12% of backlog.
Energy transition: non-fossil ~280GW (ahead of 500GW target); BESS scaling to ~200GWh+ by 2030; substation automation for solar.
Transportation: EV (30% by 2030); Vande Bharat trains — most run on Schneider equipment (target 400 trains).
Manufacturing/semicon: PLI/ISM 2.0; engaged with semicon fab investors 2.5–3 yrs (equipment + software).
Grid modernization: Tata Power Odisha; "One Digital grid" AI assistant for DISCOMs (fault/asset/SAIDI management).
new products / optionality: Dry-type Trihal transformer (33kV) localized at Baroda — for data centres, metros, commercial/residential (E4/C4F1 endurance, high seismic compliance); 170,000 units globally across 100 countries.
One Digital grid (AI grid management, cloud/on-prem, grid-AI chatbot).
margins / cost dynamics: Gross margin down 160bps on metals (Cu/Al +30%, steel +10%). Mitigation: services mix-up, modernization, pricing.
risks & watch-items: Metal-price inflation (Cu/Al/steel) squeezing gross margin — echoes Apar's caution.
Sales growth muted (+9.6% FY; Q4 flat) despite strong order intake/backlog — execution/phasing.
management quality / tone: Heavy on ESG/awards/brand; digital + services positioning; candid on metal-cost margin hit. Backlog strength (+50%) supports forward visibility.
non-obvious takeaways: Confirms the metal-price headwind independently (2nd name after Apar) — a margin watch-item for the whole OEM layer.
Differentiator is digital/grid-AI + services, not just hardware — a software-led margin lever vs pure equipment peers.
Strong orders/backlog but weak revenue conversion → watch execution/phasing in FY27.
qoq change log: Q4/FY26 (this): orders +27%, backlog +50%, sales +9.6% (Q4 ₹590cr flat); gross margin 37.5% (−160bps, metals); DC ~10–12% of backlog; Trihal dry-type localized at Baroda; One Digital grid AI; Labour-Code ₹14cr one-off.
Q1 FY27 → check: does revenue conversion improve?, margin recovery (services mix / pricing), DC backlog %, Trihal ramp.

themes.title: Data-Center & AI electrical/cooling buildout
themes.need: AI/data-center capex pulls transformers, switchgear, gensets, HVAC/cooling, optical and cabling AND a new high-margin cooling supply chain. CUMMINSIND flags DC at ~30-35% of domestic powergen with a demand surge since Oct-2025; VENUSPIPES won a ~INR185cr DC-cooling LOI; AEROFLEX building liquid-cooling skids; BLUESTARCO on DC MEP; STLTECH/NETWEB on optical + HPC/AI servers (STLTECH's DC+Enterprise mix hit 21% of Q1FY27 revenue from 1% in FY26 on record INR13,100cr quarterly order intake anchored by a $1.1bn multi-year hyperscaler deal; FY27 EBITDA-margin guide raised 20%->23% and DC+Enterprise mix guide raised 30%->50% of revenue); REDINGTON/DCI/IVALUE on GPU/AI-infra distribution. Q1FY27 added two balance-sheet-scale entrants: HCLTECH is putting up to INR 3,500cr into its own AI-datacenter business with a 50MW long-term ambition ('megawatt isn't the product, it's the anchor'), and RELIANCE disclosed a 168 MW Meta data centre at Jamnagar built on its own balance sheet.
themes.driver: DC cooling LOIs converting (VENUSPIPES, AEROFLEX); hyperscaler/colo India capex (CUMMINSIND gensets, BLUESTARCO MEP); STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler optical-connectivity deal and 2.4x QoQ order-book jump to INR18,618cr; GPU/AI-infra orders.
